mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 4.0% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% over the past 3 months signals a tight labor market, which typically leads to higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline in residential construction (HOUST) below 1300 thousand units and consumer spending (RSAFS) below 700,000 million dollars signals a weakening demand for goods and services, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS are below their thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: In the early expansion phase (indicated by INDPRO above 100 and UNRATE below 4.0%), industrial production growth signals robust economic activity, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO > 100 and UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A high consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3.5% typically triggers monetary tightening expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1300 thousand units over the past month signals a weakening real estate market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when HOUST < 1300.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of declining employment (PAYEMS) below 157,000 thousand and a low unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% signals a paradoxical labor market contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS < 157000 and UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In the late expansion phase (indicated by INDPRO above 100 and CPIAUCSL above 3.5%), high industrial production growth signals an economy near full capacity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to anticipated monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 100 and CPIAUCSL > 3.5%.
